explanation: The pieces, called tans, are five triangles in three sizes, a square and a parallelogram. Fitted together they form a square, and they can be rearranged into hundreds of silhouettes.

claims.text: A traditional tangram puzzle has seven flat pieces.
A traditional tangram does not have 5, 6 or 9 pieces.
The seven tangram pieces are five right isosceles triangles (two large, one medium and two small), a square and a parallelogram.
The tangram pieces are called tans, and together they can be arranged into a square.
Hundreds of different figures and silhouettes can be made from the tangram pieces.

evidence.restatement: The classic tangram set is cut into seven shapes; its Chinese name, qiqiao ban, means roughly 'seven boards of skill'.

claimResults.note: Answered 7 cold. The count is built into the puzzle's Chinese name.

evidence.restatement: Five, six and nine are all wrong counts for a standard tangram, which always has seven.

claimResults.note: All distractors definitely wrong; none matches a traditional variant of the puzzle.

evidence.restatement: A tangram set holds two big, one middle-sized and two little right-angled isosceles triangles, plus one square and one parallelogram.

evidence.restatement: Each tangram piece is known as a tan, and the full set fits together into one square.

claimResults.note: 'Tan' is the standard (Western) term for a piece; the dissection of a square is the puzzle's origin.

evidence.restatement: Collections of tangram problems run to thousands of distinct figures, so 'hundreds' is a safe lower statement.

claimResults.note: Published tangram books contain well over a thousand figures; 'hundreds' understates but stays true.
